subject: leftover food
title: What If You Always Left Dinner Out Overnight?

scenes.text: What if you always left dinner on the counter overnight? Reheating it won't save you.
Between 40 and 140 degrees Fahrenheit, food bacteria can double every 20 minutes.
That's why food safety experts set the limit at two hours out, or one hour above 90 degrees.
By morning, after eight hours, a few bacteria could have doubled 24 times, into millions.
Some, like staph, leave behind a toxin that heat can't destroy.
So you can kill the bacteria and still get sick from what they left. The fridge was the real cooking step.

description:
What if you always left dinner out overnight? In the danger zone of 40 to 140 degrees Fahrenheit, bacteria can double about every 20 minutes, so the USDA advises no more than two hours out, one hour above 90 degrees.
Some bacteria, such as Staphylococcus aureus, make a heat-resistant toxin, so reheating doesn't make the food safe again.
